The '''1939 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship''' was the 53rd staging of the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship]] since its establishment by the [[Gaelic Athletic Association]] in [[1887 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1887]]. The championship began on 7 May 1939 and ended on 3 September 1939.

[[Dublin GAA|Dublin]] entered the championship as the [[1938 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|defending champions]], however, they were beaten by [[Kilkenny GAA|Kilkenny]] in the [[1939 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship#Leinster Senior Hurling Championship|Leinster final]].

The [[1939 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|All-Ireland final]] was played on 3 September 1939 at [[Croke Park]] in [[Dublin]], between Kilkenny and [[Cork GAA|Cork]], in what was their first meeting in a final in [[1931 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship Final|nine years]]. Kilkenny won the match by 2–07 to 3–03 to claim their 12th championship title overall and a first title since [[1935 All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship|1935]]. The 1939 All-Ireland final remains one of the most iconic of all time.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishexaminer.com/opinion/columnists/arid-20284640.html|title=75 years ago thunder rolled at Croke Park on eve of world war|publisher=Irish Examiner|date=3 September 2014|access-date=26 August 2021|first=Enda|last=McEvoy}}</ref> Played on the day that [[United Kingdom declaration of war on Germany (1939)|Britain declared war on Germany]], the climax of the match took place during a terrific thunderstorm and earned the sobriquet of the "thunder and lightning final".<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/ireland/irish-news/epic-thunder-and-lightning-final-recalled-at-auction-in-cork-1.3023879?mode=sample&auth-failed=1&pw-origin=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.irishtimes.com%2Fnews%2Fireland%2Firish-news%2Fepic-thunder-and-lightning-final-recalled-at-auction-in-cork-1.3023879|title=Epic ‘Thunder and Lightning Final’ recalled at auction in Cork|publisher=Irish Times|date=24 March 2017|access-date=26 August 2021|first=Barry|last=Roche}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.irishtimes.com/culture/heritage/thunder-lightning-hurling-war-and-an-emergency-1.1914541?mode=sample&auth-failed=1&pw-origin=https%3A%2F%2Fwww.irishtimes.com%2Fculture%2Fheritage%2Fthunder-lightning-hurling-war-and-an-emergency-1.1914541|title=Thunder, lightning, hurling, war and an Emergency|publisher=Irish Times|date=2 September 2014|access-date=26 August 2021|first=Denis|last=Fahey}}</ref>

Kilkenny's [[Jim Langton]] was the championship's top scorer with 1–20.

==Teams==

A total of thirteen teams contested the championship, including all of the teams from the [[All-Ireland Senior Hurling Championship 1938|1938 championship]]. [[Wexford GAA|Wexford]] re-entered the championship after a one-year absence.

===Miscellaneous===

* Kilkenny's victory over Cork in the All-Ireland final was the fourth time that Kilkenny beat them by just a single point. Previous one-point wins came in 1904, 1907 and 1912.  Among the attendance was the poet [[Louis MacNeice]] who was visiting Dublin.
